lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Talk about the pictures. Make predictions.

details: Talk about the pictures activates prior knowledge and sets the scene. Students describe the different environments (city vs. countryside) and the transport they see to predict what the children will encounter.
Look for simple descriptions like "city," "bus," "trees," or "bike" and pointing to the characters walking.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Listen to the story.

details: Listen to the story develops narrative comprehension. Students listen to the first part of the story to understand the repeating pattern "I walk to school. What can I see?" and identifying the answers.
Look for attentive listening and pointing to trace the story as it progresses.

lessonPlan.topic: Student Book p31 - Act it out.

details: Act it out builds confidence and fluency. Students role-play the characters, walking on the spot and mime looking around, then saying "I can see..."
Look for clear delivery of the key phrase "What can I see?" and the appropriate waving action to the imaginary bus or bike.

Look for simple verbal expressions like "School is fun," "Friends," or "Learning."
